summary: This article explains how a honeybee colony shares its work, turns nectar into honey, pollinates plants, communicates with a dance, and helps farmers.
introduce: Show the title “Honeybees: Tiny Workers” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a big group of the same kind of animal that live together
an animal that goes out to search for food

challengeTerms.def: a natural substance in living things that speeds up a chemical change
to share information or ideas with others
moving pollen from one flower to another so the plant can make seeds

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that bees are more helpful than harmful to people? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why farmers depend on honeybees.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review colony, nectar, and forager, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses enzyme, communicate, and pollination to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
